articles.title: DAC Clears High Mobility Vehicles, Light Multi Role Helicopters , Gun Systems and Drones for Indian Army
articles.text:
The Defence Acquisition Council (DAC), chaired by Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh on October 26, 2026, accorded Acceptance of Necessity (AoN) i.e. in-principle administrative to various capital acquisition proposals of the Defence Forces at an estimated cost of about Rs 2,12,000 crore. For the Indian Army, approval was accorded for the procurement of High Mobility Vehicles (HMV), Self-Propelled Tracked Gun System, Gun Shot Response System (GSRS), Light Multi Role Helicopters (LMRH), Very Short-Range Air Defence System (VSHORADS), Platform Based Counter Unmanned Aerial System (C-UAS), Unmanned Aerial System Brick Long Range, Surveillance UAV, Integrated Surveillance and Strike System and Long Range Kamikaze Drone System.
The HMVs will enhance operational capabilities, logistic support and mobility in challenging terrains. The Self-Propelled Tracked Gun System will provide matching mobility and firepower to mechanised formations. The GSRS will serve as a force multiplier providing real-time situational awareness of the forces. The LMRH will be used by both the Indian Army and the Indian Air Force for Reconnaissance and Surveillance, Combat, Search and Rescue of troops, Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief etc. The VSHORADS will engage new generation small size aerial threats, while C-UAS will enhance survivability of Tanks in the modern battlefield. The Surveillance and Drone Systems will enhance the surveillance and targeting capabilities of the Indian Army.
For the Indian Navy, approval was given for the procurement of Active Offboard Decoy System (AODS) and other major Naval platforms. The AODS will enhance the credibility of anti-missiles defence, especially against modern anti-ship missiles of adversaries. The indigenously designed and constructed major Naval platforms will possess modern-day warfare capabilities and enhance the combat capability of the Navy.
For the Indian Air Force, approval was accorded for the procurement of Helicopters, Air Defence Systems, Weapons and Mobile X-Band Doppler Weather Radar System to enhance the air defence and war fighting capabilities. The procurement of Special Utility Helicopters will help the Indian Air Force to meet the important air transport requirements. The X-Band Doppler Weather Radar System will provide high-resolution, localised weather surveillance in forward areas.
Out of the total AoNs accorded, approximately 82% of the procurements will be made from the Indian Industry.

Israeli MoD press release

This agreement marks another important step in strengthening the operational capabilities of the Cyprus Naval Command and enhancing its capacity to respond to maritime security challenges. The new OPV, alongside the upgraded OPV IOANNIDES, will support expanded patrol, surveillance, and search-and-rescue missions. By strengthening their capabilities and deepening their partnership, the two countries reaffirm their commitment to regional stability.

articles.title: Anthropic vs OpenAI: How Claude maker’s growth is challenging ChatGPT ahead of IPO
articles.text: Anthropic has emerged as a strong challenger to OpenAI in the race to sell artificial intelligence to businesses, with its revenue rising sharply as demand for its Claude models grows. But investors weighing the two companies must look beyond sales growth to understand which business is better placed to deliver returns.Anthropic, which unveiled its initial public offering filing on Monday, reported revenue of $16.29 billion in the first half of 2026. OpenAI, the maker of ChatGPT, reported quarterly revenue of $6.7 billion in the second quarter, according to Reuters.The figures suggest Anthropic has built strong momentum in the enterprise market, where companies pay to use AI for software development, data analysis and other business tasks. But the comparison is not straightforward because the two companies account for some sales through cloud partners differently.OpenAI has also been expanding rapidly and remains a major player in the consumer AI market. The competition between the two companies is therefore likely to depend on their ability to attract paying customers, control computing costs and turn revenue growth into cash.Revenue growth favours AnthropicAnthropic’s revenue rose to $4.59 billion in 2025 from $386 million in 2024, according to its IPO filing. Revenue for the first six months of 2026 reached $16.29 billion.The company has benefited from growing demand for Claude, particularly its coding tools, which help software developers write, check and fix code. Its products are also used by businesses seeking to automate work and build AI-powered applications.OpenAI, meanwhile, has expanded beyond ChatGPT into business software, developer tools and AI agents. Reuters reported in October that OpenAI’s annualised revenue run rate for September was close to $50 billion, lower than the nearly $70 billion figure it had previously indicated to investors.An annualised revenue run rate estimates a full year’s revenue by extending a recent period’s sales. It is not the same as revenue actually earned over a year.Also Read: Anthropic IPO: 5 jaw-dropping numbers investors need to know about $1.5 trillion public offerIt should be noted that Anthropic records the full value of certain sales made through cloud marketplaces as revenue and records the platform fees separately. OpenAI does not include some similar cloud-partner sales in its revenue figures.This difference makes it difficult to determine which company has the larger underlying business from headline revenue alone.The profitability questionRapid revenue growth has not removed the financial risks facing either company.Anthropic reported an operating loss of $693 million in the first half of 2026, according to its IPO filing. Its reported net loss was much larger, at $80.7 billion, largely because of a non-cash accounting charge linked to the increased estimated value of bonds that may eventually convert into company shares.The operating loss provides a better indication of the gap between the company’s operating income and expenses during the period, although it does not by itself show how much cash the company generated or used.OpenAI also faces heavy spending requirements. Reuters reported in September, citing a Financial Times report, that the company expected to use about $278 billion in cash between 2026 and 2030 as it invests in computing power and infrastructure.The figures are not directly comparable because they cover different periods and measures. However, they underline the challenge facing both companies: advanced AI requires large investments in computing capacity, data centres, chips and research before the companies can generate sustainable returns.Computing costs and Big Tech dependenceAnthropic depends heavily on Amazon and Google for computing infrastructure and access to business customers. Both companies are also investors in Anthropic and compete with it in AI.Reuters reported that Amazon and Google’s cloud marketplaces accounted for 47% of Anthropic’s sales to customers in 2025. These relationships help Claude reach businesses already using their cloud services, but they also expose Anthropic to dependence on a small number of powerful partners.OpenAI has its own infrastructure requirements and strategic partnerships, including its close relationship with Microsoft. It has also been committing substantial sums to secure computing capacity for future AI development.The companies’ ability to manage these commitments will be important as competition increases. If AI usage grows more slowly than expected, large infrastructure obligations could weigh on cash flow. If demand continues to rise rapidly, access to computing power could become a competitive advantage.Also Read : Anthropic IPO: What should investors consider when valuing the AI company? Aswath Damodaran explainsValuation will determine investor returnsBoth companies are seeking valuations that reflect expectations of enormous future growth.Anthropic has been valued by some investors at around $1.5 trillion in recent discussions, below expectations of about $2 trillion reported earlier. OpenAI has also been linked to a potential valuation exceeding $1.4 trillion in recent fundraising talks, according to Reuters.These are reported private-market valuations and fundraising discussions, not necessarily the final prices at which either company’s shares will be offered to public investorA higher valuation does not automatically mean a company is better placed. Investors must assess how much future growth is already reflected in the price and whether the company can deliver the revenue and profits needed to justify it.Anthropic’s upcoming IPO could provide a useful benchmark for valuing AI businesses. OpenAI’s eventual listing, expected later, could give investors another opportunity to compare the companies using more detailed financial disclosures.Which business is better placed?Anthropic currently has a strong case based on its rapid revenue growth and position in business AI, particularly coding. Its latest disclosures also give investors a clearer view of its operating performance and infrastructure commitments.OpenAI has a broad consumer presence through ChatGPT, a growing enterprise business and significant financial and technology partnerships. Its scale gives it opportunities to sell AI products across a wide range of users and applications.

articles.title: India to Push Defence Cooperation at 13th ADMM-Plus in Philippines
articles.text:
Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh will lead the Indian delegation at the 13th Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Defence Ministers’ Meeting (ADMM) – Plus at Cebu, Philippines from October 28 to 29, 2026. He will address the forum on ‘Exchange of Views on Regional and International Security Issues’.
On the sidelines of ADMM-Plus, Raksha Mantri will hold bilateral meetings with his counterparts of participating countries. He will review the ongoing defence ties with the nations, and explore ways to further strengthen strategic partnerships.
The ADMM is the highest defence consultative and cooperative mechanism in ASEAN. ADMM-Plus is a platform for ASEAN member states (Brunei, Cambodia, Indonesia, Lao PDR, Malaysia, Myanmar, Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, Timor Leste and Vietnam) and its eight Dialogue Partners (India, US, China, Russia, Japan, South Korea, Australia and New Zealand) to strengthen security and defence cooperation.
India became the dialogue partner of ASEAN in 1992 and the inaugural ADMM-Plus was convened in Hanoi, Vietnam on October 12, 2010. Since 2017, ADMM-Plus Ministers have been meeting annually to bolster defence cooperation amongst ASEAN and the Plus countries.
The Philippines is the chair of ADMM-Plus for 2026. Under the construct of ADMM-Plus, India is co-chairing the Experts Working Group on Counter-Terrorism with Malaysia for the cycle 2024-2027. India’s active participation in the ADMM-Plus mechanisms underscores the deepening defence diplomacy in Southeast Asia under the Act East policy, aimed at ensuring peace, stability and collective growth in the region.

articles.title: Paytm Q2 Results: Profit rockets 976% YoY to Rs 226 crore, revenue jumps 28%
articles.text: Fintech major Paytm on Monday reported 976% year-on-year (YoY) growth in its consolidated net profit at Rs 226 crore for the second quarter of FY27. The same stood at Rs 21 crore in the year-ago quarter. Revenue from operations in the reporting period rose 28% YoY to Rs 2,648 crore.However, on a sequential basis, profit rose just 3% from Rs 220 crore posted in the preceding June quarter.The sharp increase in reported profit was also helped by a lower exceptional charge. Paytm recorded exceptional expenses of Rs 4 crore during the September quarter, compared with Rs 190 crore a year earlier. Profit before exceptional items increased 9% to Rs 229 crore.EBITDA for the quarter surged 90% to Rs 270 crore from Rs 142 crore a year earlier. The company's EBITDA margin improved to 10% from 7% in the year-ago quarter, reflecting higher revenue and improved operating leverage.Paytm said its growing merchant network, expansion of financial services distribution and adoption of artificial intelligence across operations contributed to the improvement in profitability.Financial servicesRevenue from the distribution of financial services rose 49% year-on-year to Rs 912 crore from Rs 611 crore, emerging as one of Paytm's fastest-growing businesses.The company has been expanding its merchant and consumer loan distribution operations through partnerships with financial institutions.Its number of key financial services customers increased 35% to 8.8 lakh from 6.5 lakh a year earlier. Repeat borrowers accounted for more than half of merchant loan disbursements.Paytm said growth in merchant lending was supported by an expanding customer base eligible for loans, higher engagement and increasing participation from lending partners.The company also reported improvement in its consumer lending operations, including personal loans and Paytm Postpaid, a credit line on UPI.Paytm expects higher default loss guarantee (DLG) costs from the December quarter as it expands loan distribution under agreements with lending partners. However, the company expects EBITDA to continue improving despite these upfront expenses.Payments businessRevenue from payment services increased 25% year-on-year to Rs 1,434 crore from Rs 1,146 crore. Gross merchandise value (GMV), representing the total value of payments made to merchants through Paytm's platform, increased 26% to Rs 7.1 lakh crore from Rs 5.7 lakh crore.The number of merchants paying for subscriptions, including payment devices, rose to 1.64 crore from 1.37 crore a year earlier, an addition of 27 lakh.Net payment revenue stood at Rs 644 crore, an increase of 8% on a reported basis. Excluding Payments Infrastructure Development Fund incentives, comparable growth was 21%.The company's payment processing margin remained above four basis points, supported by growth in merchant payment instruments that generate fees and improved pricing.Paytm also reported its sixth consecutive quarter of market share gains in consumer payments. Monthly transacting users increased to 8.5 crore from 7.5 crore a year earlier.The company's UPI gross transaction value grew 42%, compared with industry growth of 19%, according to figures cited by Paytm.UPI merchant chargesPaytm said a proposed merchant discount rate (MDR) on certain UPI transactions could provide additional revenue and profit opportunities.The company referred to a recently notified framework for charges on select merchant UPI payments, with implementation expected after Diwali on a date yet to be announced.Based on its existing payment mix, Paytm estimates the proposed charges could increase its overall payment processing margin by around 2.5 basis points.The company said any additional revenue from UPI MDR would supplement its existing payments and financial services businesses.AI investments and cost efficiencyPaytm's indirect expenses increased 14% YoY to Rs 1,209 crore, growing slower than its 28% revenue expansion.Consequently, indirect expenses declined to 46% of revenue from 52% a year earlier.The company said AI-driven productivity improvements were helping it manage customer acquisition, servicing, fraud prevention and operational costs. Revenue from marketing services increased 26% to Rs 287 crore from Rs 228 crore.

articles.title: Former Presidential ADC Major Rishabh Singh Sambyal Enters Fashion Space
articles.text:
Former President’s Aide-de-Camp Major Rishabh Singh Sambyal has made yet another big step in his transition away from the Army by participating in a new brand collaboration with Indian streetwear label Bonkers Corner.
A “Major Rishabh X Bonkers” campaign currently features on the label’s website, with Rishabh modelling a black zip-up hoodie with star motifs and loose-fitting trousers as part of the Bonkers Corner brand’s wider list of highlighted collaborations and collections.
The presence of the former aide-de-camp in the post confirms that a deal has indeed taken place but the financial details and structure of the deal remain undisclosed.
Rishabh was propelled to national prominence after being named as Aide-de-Camp to President Droupadi Murmu and his appearances with the Head of State at various events generated significant social media engagement. He left the Army in 2026 after a dozen years of service which saw him hold posts with the Jat Regiment and 4 Para Special Forces before being appointed to his role as the President’s ADC. He cited family reasons for his decision to retire.
The new collaboration with Bonkers Corner marks the latest phase in the ex-ADC’s transition out of the Army after it was announced in September this year that he would begin to monetise his social media following by introducing paid Instagram subscriptions to his account. This too created controversy with some claiming that it was inappropriate for someone who had gained his fame as a soldier to exploit his following in this way. However others pointed to the fact that he had served his country and was now free to take up whatever opportunities were available to him as a private citizen so long as he observed relevant laws and regulations.
Riding on his popularity as the President’s ADC, the ex-military personnel has once again demonstrated his versatility by starring in a fashion editorial for Bonkers Corner. According to the label’s website, it is a home-grown Indian streetwear brand which provides modern, unisex clothing. Swavlamban 2026 was held in New Delhi on 26-27 October and included the Indian Navy, defence companies, startups and research organisations. This gives an opportunity for new developers to show off their concepts which could provide future solutions to armed forces.
D-Propulse now faces the challenge of proving their system is more than just a concept and that the propulsion technology can provide a reliable integrated interceptor. Flight tests, guidance and controlled interception tests would need to be completed before the system could be assessed.

AUSTIN, Texas—Formula 1 returned to US shores this weekend with its annual visit to the Circuit of the Americas in Austin, Texas. Once in danger of falling off the calendar due to a lack of interest, it’s now one of the most popular tracks on the calendar and, of the US’s three races, it's the one the real fans mostly attend.

Unlike Miami or Las Vegas, which race on temporary street circuits, COTA is a permanent race track with plenty of run-off areas instead of concrete walls. Designed by motorcycle racer Kevin Schwanz—Herman Tilke’s company did only the buildings and infrastructure, contrary to popular belief—the track combines a mix of corner speeds with challenging turn sequences, a few heavy braking zones, and plenty of elevation changes.

It’s a place Ars knows rather intimately by now. We’ve driven it in everything from an Audi TT-S to a Corvette ZR1 to a bicycle, and that’s just in the real world. Over the years, we’ve been there for F1 to learn about how the sport puts together its broadcasts, how Pirelli designs its tires, and how various tech partners help teams manage their data and strategies. We even saw the race through a neophyte’s eyes. And that’s just F1—we’ve logged many hours there with the World Endurance Championship and IMSA for the Lone Star Le Mans races in sweaty September.

articles.title: Could China’s KJ-3000 AWACS Support Pakistan Without Entering Its Airspace?
articles.text:
China’s ability to conduct airborne early warning could cause issues for IAF operations during a future conflict against Pakistan. This is especially the case if the PLAAF are able to offer intelligence and surveillance support without entering the fight. Simplistic radar models can give us an idea of how this could affect the overall situation.
For example, a PAF Saab Erieye conducting airborne early warning operations in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa could detect Indian LCA and Su-30MKI aircraft near the border. However, they will not be able to maintain a stable track. Whilst they will not have a weapon grade track, they will have given early warning to Controllers which may allow them to send their fighter aircraft to that general area.
This detection will not provide the PAF with track or any information to engage with missiles. How useful the Erieye is will depend on how quickly the PAF can create a better picture.
Secondly, a scenario where three Chinese KJ-3000 aircraft are conducting airborne early warning operations over Aksai Chin. The aircraft can be seen to track the Indian fighters including a Rafale conducting operations over Jammu.
The KJ-3000 is still in development and there is no information available to suggest that they are currently in operation in this capacity. We do not have full details about their radar capabilities, EW resilience and how well they can provide targeting information. This should be seen as an assessment of future capabilities.
This creates a strategic issue from an operational standpoint. If China are providing surveillance support during a limited conflict between India and Pakistan, this puts the Indian leadership in a tricky situation. They may have to decide whether to accept this support or risk escalation by viewing the Chinese military aircraft as threats. Whilst we cannot assume that they will remain calm, it may affect how Indian operations are planned.
The most useful benefit to the PAF would be having early warning from Chinese sensors. It would be useful if this information could be used within the PAF’s C2 systems to provide useful information to the fighters. Detection alone would not guarantee they can intercept.
This could cause more uncertainty for the Indians. If they have to plan around an extra surveillance network they may be uncertain how exposed their aircraft will be.
Stealth could cause issues for the adversary detecting and tracking your aircraft. However, they won’t be undetectable by all radars. India can use airborne surveillance, EW and improve their networked operations.
